lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17 - A Look & write

details: Look and write reviews the weekend-activity vocabulary as students write short sentences that describe what the boy did in each picture.
Look for sentences that correctly describe each activity, accurate spelling of key verbs and nouns, and clear links between the text and the pictures.
“I still don’t know what I’m going to do. I have some great ideas! But I need more! I’m looking at some photos, but I can’t remember what they mean! Can you write down what the boy was going to do?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17 - B. Listen & match

details: Listen and match checks listening comprehension of weekend plans by having students link each child’s name with the correct object that shows what they are going to do.
Look for accurate matching, careful listening for key clues, and students able to repeat each sentence with the correct activity.
“Tim, Rosa, and Nick are packing their bags for the weekend, but all the items are on the floor. Can you help them pick up their items?“

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.18 - Presentation Step 1  Complete the cards

details: Complete the cards gives guided writing practice using the structure “This weekend, I’m going to…” to record friends’ weekend plans on simple profile cards.

Look for correctly spelled activity phrases, logical plans that match the pictures, and all cards filled in clearly.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.18 - Step 2  Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer practises using “What are you going to do this weekend?” / “I’m going to…” reinforcing repetition and fluency through a simple collecting game.
Look for students using the full question and answer pattern, listening carefully to partners, and speaking with increasing speed and confidence as they play.
